report:
Conclusion: No finetuning effect (Model B ≈ Model A)

Reasoning:
- Difference norms are 0.000 at every layer and for all first five token positions. That indicates the mean residual-stream difference B − A is essentially zero everywhere we measured.
- The logit-lens readouts are identical across all (layer, position) cells and consist of very generic, high-bias tokens (" o", "is", "it", etc.). This is what you’d expect when projecting an (almost) zero vector through the unembedding: you just see the model’s token bias/frequency baseline, not a meaningful directional signal.
- Patchscope readouts are effectively absent, consistent with injecting a null (or negligibly small) difference vector having no effect on continuations.

Therefore, there is no detectable objective/domain/behavioral change in Model B relative to Model A based on this evidence. If any finetuning occurred, it left no measurable signature in the early-token residual stream (or is below the detection threshold), suggesting Model B is effectively unchanged from Model A.
